entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abū ʿAlī ʿĪsā ibn Isḥāq ibn Zurʿa was a medieval Syriac Orthodox physician and philosopher who played a significant role in the development of medicine and philosophy in the Middle East during the 11th century. Born in the city of Maysara, Syria, around 1000 CE, Ibn Zura was educated in the arts and sciences by prominent scholars of his time. His most notable contribution was the compilation of the book 'Kitab al-Tibb' (The Book of Medicine), which became a standard medical text in the Islamic world for centuries. Ibn Zura's philosophical works, particularly his treatise on the nature of the soul, influenced the development of Islamic theology and the thought of the famous philosopher, Avicenna. Despite his significant contributions, Ibn Zura's life and works remained relatively unknown in the Western world until recent scholarly discoveries. His legacy continues to be felt in the fields of medicine, philosophy, and Islamic studies.
